hypothesis: The evaluator now has a useful light cavity-cost signal, but delayed-payoff lines such as donation or building upward before a Quad can still be starved if temporarily lower-ranked branches receive too few search selections. Changing only DAG child-selection exploitation may improve KO performance by preserving or pruning those branches more appropriately.

selection_rule.implementation: child rank i = floor(((-ln(U))/exploitation) mod child_count)
selection_rule.default: ln(2), which before finite-list wrap corresponds to approximately 50%, 25%, 12.5%, ... across successive ranks
selection_rule.direction: smaller exploitation explores lower-ranked children more; larger exploitation concentrates more strongly on current high-ranked children
selection_rule.finite_list_note: modulo wrap means the exact finite-list probabilities are not the infinite geometric distribution

screen.interpretation: Both extremes were harmful. The tied screening leaders were 40% and 55%, but nearby points did not reproduce the advantage, so screening alone did not identify a stable monotonic direction.

validation.interpretation: The 40% exploration-heavy screen winner regressed exactly to 40:40. The 55% slightly greedier candidate remained positive at 46:34 and is the pre-fixed finalist. This does not establish a general monotonic benefit of greedier search; it only justifies confirming the fixed 55% setting.

fixed_finalist.selection_reason: fresh validation winner, fixed before confirmation

protocol.speculation: SevenBag after visible preview, never true hidden future
protocol.incoming_garbage: 10 hidden-hole scenarios while under observed pressure
protocol.search_rng: deterministic and separate from authority RNG

promotion_rule: No promotion from screening or validation. The fixed 55% finalist must beat H9 in fresh confirmation. If it does not, keep H9 and stop scalar exploitation tuning rather than inventing intermediate values post-hoc.
